facts.text: Grand Coteau began when two nuns of the Religious of the Sacred Heart founded a convent and school that became the Academy of the Sacred Heart.
Historic homes in Grand Coteau feature Creole cottages built of cypress, fronted by four- or six-column galleries and sometimes Greek Revival or Victorian filigree.
The town's name changed from St. Charles Town to Grand Coteau after the schools around the Academy grew into a community.
During the Civil War, the Ninety-ninth Infantry Regiment of Illinois fought the Battle of Grand Coteau, a skirmish that drew Union troops to the area.
Although thousands of Union soldiers camped around the Academy during the war, the school itself remained untouched.
Grand Coteau preserves Victorian architecture from its mid‑19th‑century boom, with buildings that showcase the era's ornate detailing.
